t: Proclaimed by Peter the Great in 1721 after defeating Sweden, the Russian Empire grew to cover some 22.8 million square kilometres.
It spread Russian rule from the Baltic to the Pacific and Central Asia, and freed some 23 million serfs in 1861.
Autocracy, rural discontent and the strain of the First World War brought revolution and Nicholas II's abdication in 1917.
dyk: Before the Battle of Tsushima in 1905, Russia's Baltic Fleet sailed some 18,000 nautical miles around the world, only to be annihilated by Japan.
ev: Peter I begins building Saint Petersburg on conquered Swedish territory
Peter's reformed army defeats Charles XII of Sweden at Poltava
The Senate proclaims Peter I Emperor of All Russia after the Treaty of Nystad
Napoleon's Grande Armée invades Russia and is destroyed in the winter retreat
Alexander II's Emancipation Edict frees some 23 million privately owned serfs
Construction of the Trans-Siberian Railway begins
Defeat at Tsushima and revolution force Nicholas II to issue the October Manifesto
Nicholas II abdicates after the Petrograd garrison mutinies
